narrator.name: Narrator
narrator.note: The evangelist Matthew; orderly, measured storytelling, including his own Scripture citations.

jesus.name: Jesus
jesus.note: Jesus of Nazareth; calm authority, teaching in parables, commanding and healing.

disciples.name: The disciples
disciples.note: Jesus' followers speaking together; questioning, practical and anxious, slow to understand, awed in the boat.

peter.name: Peter
peter.note: Spokesman of the twelve; impulsive, frightened on the water, firm in his confession, then presuming to rebuke.

pharisees-and-scribes.name: The scribes and Pharisees
pharisees-and-scribes.note: Religious authorities from Jerusalem; fault-finding and accusing.

syrophoenician-woman.name: The woman of Canaan
syrophoenician-woman.note: A Gentile mother begging for her possessed daughter; crying out, humble and quick-witted.

1.t: Then came to him from Jerusalem scribes and Pharisees, saying:

2.t: Why do thy disciples transgress the tradition of the ancients? For they wash not their hands when they eat bread.

3.t: But he answering, said to them:
Why do you also transgress the commandment of God for your tradition? For God said:

4.t: Honour thy father and mother: And: He that shall curse father or mother, let him die the death.

5.t: But you say: Whosoever shall say to father or mother, The gift whatsoever proceedeth from me, shall profit thee.

6.t: And he shall not honour his father or his mother: and you have made void the commandment of God for your tradition.

7.t: Hypocrites, well hath Isaias prophesied of you, saying:

8.t: This people honoureth me with their lips: but their heart is far from me.

9.t: And in vain do they worship me, teaching doctrines and commandments of men.

10.t: And having called together the multitudes unto him, he said to them:

11.t: Not that which goeth into the mouth defileth a man: but what cometh out of the mouth, this defileth a man.

12.t: Then came his disciples, and said to him:
Dost thou know that the Pharisees, when they heard this word, were scandalized?

13.t: Every plant which my heavenly Father hath not planted, shall be rooted up.

14.t: Let them alone: they are blind, and leaders of the blind. And if the blind lead the blind, both fall into the pit.

15.t: And Peter answering, said to him:

16.t: Are you also yet without understanding?

17.t: Do you not understand, that whatsoever entereth into the mouth, goeth into the belly, and is cast out into the privy?

18.t: But the things which proceed out of the mouth, come forth from the heart, and those things defile a man.

19.t: For from the heart come forth evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, fornications, thefts, false testimonies, blasphemies.

20.t: These are the things that defile a man. But to eat with unwashed hands doth not defile a man.

21.t: And Jesus went from thence, and retired into the coast of Tyre and Sidon.

22.t: And behold a woman of Canaan who came out of those coasts, crying out, said to him:
Have mercy on me, O Lord, thou son of David: my daughter is grievously troubled by a devil.

23.t: Who answered her not a word. And his disciples came and besought him, saying:
Send her away, for she crieth after us:

24.t: I was not sent but to the sheep, that are lost of the house of Israel.

25.t: But she came and adored him, saying:

26.t: It is not good to take the bread of the children, and to cast it to the dogs.

27.t: Yea, Lord; for the whelps also eat of the crumbs that fall from the table of their masters.

28.t: Then Jesus answering, said to her:
O woman, great is thy faith: be it done to thee as thou wilt:
and her daughter was cured from that hour.

29.t: And when Jesus had passed away from thence, he came nigh the sea of Galilee: and going up into a mountain, he sat there.

30.t: And there came to him great multitudes, having with them the dumb, the blind, the lame, the maimed, and many others: and they cast them down at his feet, and he healed them:

31.t: So that the multitudes marvelled seeing the dumb speak, the lame walk, the blind see: and they glorified the God of Israel.

32.t: And Jesus called together his disciples, and said:
I have compassion on the multitudes, because they continue with me now three days, and have not what to eat, and I will not send them away fasting, lest they faint in the way.

33.t: And the disciples say unto him:
Whence then should we have so many loaves in the desert, as to fill so great a multitude?

34.t: Seven, and a few little fishes.

35.t: And he commanded the multitude to sit down upon the ground.

36.t: And taking the seven loaves and the fishes, and giving thanks, he brake, and gave to his disciples, and the disciples gave to the people.

37.t: And they did all eat, and had their fill. And they took up seven baskets full, of what remained of the fragments.

38.t: And they that did eat, were four thousand men, beside children and women.

39.t: And having dismissed the multitude, he went up into a boat, and came into the coasts of Magedan.
